what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Good engineering has a presence you can feel; agent teams make the gaps show, and pushing the limits shows where to fix them.
sections.para: Good engineering shows in speed, quality and where bugs occur. Many agent teams behave like many human teams, slowed by engineering gaps, but agents absorb the overhead quietly. The PHP newsroom pushed sgit to 228,000-file vaults and split a repository whose every release touched about 1,936 files; this site still touches about 1,588.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Nine lines: the presence, reviewing by side effects, teams, hidden overhead, sgit, the split, this site's gap, schedules, explorer to villager.
sections.para: You can feel good engineering. Agents are reviewed by their side effects. Many agent teams get in each other's way like human teams. Agents hide the overhead. sgit went from 566 to 31.7 seconds a pull. A split cut files per change to one to three. This site still rewrites 1,588. Scheduled agents hold the level; refactor when innovation slows.

sections.label: The feel of it
sections.line: Good engineering has a weight and a smoothness; it shows in the side effects, which is how the author now reviews agents.
sections.para: Like a mechanic hearing an engine, someone who knows good architecture and code can feel it: speed, quality, effectiveness, bugs at the edges. The author reviews AI work mostly by its side effects and reads code to give direction, in an environment with many focused agents and more non-functional requirements met than usual.

sections.label: Many agent teams behave like many human teams
sections.line: Several agent teams on one repository collide like human teams: version races, duplicate records, tests coupled to content.
sections.para: Without shared engineering, conventions and workflows, teams undo each other's work. In one day here: two version races, the same review filed twice by two agents, and a correction that broke another agent's test. None is an agent bug; each is an engineering gap. The PHP newsroom logged 28 collision messages in three days before its split.

sections.label: The overhead you don't see
sections.line: Agents absorb the overhead and tokens are cheap, so waste hides: every release touched every page in both newsrooms.
sections.para: The PHP newsroom stamped its version on every page, so every release touched a median of 1,936 files, at up to 77 releases a day. This site touched a median of 1,588 files over its last 25 releases, usually for one article. Nobody decided it; it is what happens when nobody watches side effects and the cost is paid in tokens.

sections.label: Push the limits, and watch what breaks
sections.line: The PHP vaults pushed sgit until it broke, and three releases in five days fixed what the newsroom measured.
sections.para: A 29,861-file vault outgrew the server's listing: a 90.8-second timeout and failed pushes. Pack vaults in 0.24.0 brought the listing to 0.73 seconds and clones from 827 to 95. A field report led to 0.25.0, commits from 12 minutes to 25 seconds, and 0.26.0, pulls from 566 to 31.7 seconds on 228,000 files. A paused team resumes weeks later.

sections.label: Constant velocity
sections.line: Experts set the level, scheduled agents hold it, and technical debt is paid in days rather than quarters.
sections.para: Experts in design, communication, engineering and architecture can enforce quality without doing the work, knowing when to stop and fix. Schedules make it constant: the librarian, security, the ontologist, the desk and the conductor wake, check and act. Security raised 43 advisories, fact-check holds 162 tickets, the correspondent caught 18 errors. Debt gets paid quickly.

sections.label: Explorer, then villager
sections.line: Explorer coding while innovating, then a villager refactor: the PHP newsroom's split into six, and this site's turn next.
sections.para: When innovation slows, move from explorer to villager coding and refactor. The PHP newsroom split along who writes and how often: two decisions reversed, nine introduced bugs caught, two old bugs found, and now one to three files a change; its references site is the next round. This site's 1,588 files a release and version races say it is due its own.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: Feeling is experience, not a metric; counts are medians from git; sgit timings are the teams' own; the ranking is an opinion.
sections.para: That good engineering can be felt is experience; the numbers show the feeling pointed at something real. Counts are medians from git history on 27 October and the PHP figures come from its own briefs. sgit timings are the newsroom's and CLI team's measurements in cloud sessions. Calling this environment one of the most effective is the author's opinion.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: The PHP newsroom's briefs on pack vaults, sgit 0.25.0 and 0.26.0, and the split, sgit's release notes, and git history.
sections.para: The PHP October 2026 newsroom's briefs on moving a vault to pack mode, the field report to the sgit CLI team on 0.25.0, the 0.26.0 brief, the proposal and challenges report for splitting one repository into six; sgit's 0.26.0 release notes; and the git history of newsroom.sgit.ai and the six PHP repositories, counted on 27 October 2026.
